title: Minneapolis players and first meeting Art Tatum
summary: He recalls Raymond Valentine and a Hines-like pianist in Minneapolis, and says he met Tatum when with McKinney's.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: When I came out here... Let me see... I did a lot of shit before that time. Seems that I stayed around Minneapolis for a little while. Oh, there used to be a good tenor player around there named Raymond(?) Valentine. You ever hear of him?
He got to make some records, I think, for Gennett.

Let me see if there was anybody else around there. There was a good piano player, but now I can't think of his name. He played like Earl Hines. He was backing the numbers and he got rich real quick, and that ended his career playing, you know what I mean? But he was a good piano player.
You hadn't run into Art Tatum yet, though.
No, I didn't run into Art Tatum until I was with McKinney's Cotton Pickers. I ran into him in 1933 or '34. Then we did a lot of playing together.
